documentation.topic: Monad chain id and contract configuration
documentation.documentedBehavior: Publishes the canonical Monad testnet addresses and six-decimal aUSDC
documentation.limitations: Unauthenticated endpoint. It states no documentation version and does not describe ABIs, lifecycle rules or gateway acceptance.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedBehavior: Creates an A-Pass for wallet{address, chain}. expirationTime is a required Unix-seconds timestamp. Country tags are derived from identityDataList[].issuingCountryISO2 since v5.5.
documentation.limitations: The chapter documents the gateway request contract only. It publishes no Solidity interface and does not state whether a contract address is accepted.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedBehavior: Described generically as the "A-Pass receiving wallet address". No EOA-only restriction is stated anywhere in the chapter.
documentation.limitations: Absence of a restriction is not a documented guarantee of acceptance. Only the Validator chapter explicitly contemplates contract addresses, and it does so for the registrar role, not for A-Pass issuance.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: POST /atoken/launch with chain, token_name, token_symbol, decimals, admin_address, rule, icon, optional callback_url
documentation.documentedBehavior: Submits an application for a standard A-Token. The rule object carries allowed_group, allowed_sub_group, min_tier, min_sub_tier and, since v5.5 (2026-07-13), is_black_list and countries.
documentation.limitations: The documentation describes the REST contract. It publishes no on-chain factory ABI, so no documented launch selector exists to compare against bytecode.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: GET /atoken/query_apply_status/{requestId}; optional apply-result webhook via callback_url
documentation.documentedBehavior: Submission returns only a requestId. An issuance is successful only when applyStatus becomes ISSUED.
documentation.limitations: Terminal failure states are observable through the same endpoint but their remediation is not documented.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.topic: Mint and burn role semantics on issued A-Tokens
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: MINTER_ROLE, granted by admin_address after ISSUED
documentation.documentedBehavior: For a standard A-Token the admin wallet grants MINTER_ROLE to the chosen minter, and only then may that minter mint. For a Wrapped A-Token, MINTER_ROLE is granted to the access_core contract, which locks the origin token and mints 1:1.
documentation.limitations: BURN authority is never documented for a standard A-Token. The documentation states what MINTER_ROLE permits for minting only.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: rule object (compliance rule) evaluated against A-Pass attributes
documentation.documentedBehavior: The platform uses the token's rule together with the holder's A-Pass attributes (tier, subTier, group, subGroup and country tags) to determine whether a wallet may receive or transfer that A-Token. min_tier admits a user whose tier is strictly greater than the configured value.
documentation.limitations: No Solidity policy interface is published. `canTransfer(address,address,address,uint256)` appears nowhere in the documentation; Mordant's ICleanversePolicy is inferred from deployed bytecode, not from a documented ABI.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: Wrapped A-Token flow; access_core resolved via the supported A-Token list endpoint
documentation.documentedBehavior: A wrapped asset is minted 1:1 against a locked origin token when a whitelisted institution address funds the deposit address.
documentation.limitations: Per-network aUSDC addresses and decimals are not published as a static table; they must be discovered through the query endpoints.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedAbiOrEndpoint: chain slug "monad" in the supported-network lists
documentation.documentedBehavior: monad is a documented, case-insensitive chain slug for A-Pass and A-Token operations, alongside solana, base, avalanche, arbitrum, ethereum, polygon, bsc, hashkey and platon.
documentation.limitations: The documentation publishes no Monad chain id and no Monad contract addresses. Those come from the runtime configuration endpoint, which states no version.

documentation.documentationVersionSource: Page title "Cleanverse API v5.6 - Integration Documentation" and the version-history table, whose latest entry is v5.6 dated 2026-07-21
documentation.documentedBehavior: Pools are on-chain addresses registered with the APass Compliance Validator contract. grant and register require an EIP-191 owner_signature over the lowercase chain slug concatenated with the lowercase hex address. Signed grant is explicitly intended for smart-contract addresses exposing Ownable.owner().
documentation.limitations: No Validator contract address and no Solidity ABI are published for any network, so an on-chain ICviVerifier cannot be written from the documentation.

Country tags are derived from identityDataList[].issuingCountryISO2 since v5.5. LIMITS: The chapter documents the gateway request contract only. It publishes no Solidity interface and does not state whether a contract address is accepted.
comparisons.observedSignatureOrBehavior: isValidAPass(address) answers and returns false for addresses without a record
comparisons.impactOnMordant: CleanverseAPassVerifier depends on this exact selector and on a false answer for absent records. The deployment behaves that way; the documented guarantee is unread.
comparisons.smallestSponsorQuestion: Which documentation page and version defines isValidAPass(address) and its behavior for expired or absent records on Monad?

comparisons.topic: aUSDC role-gated mint and burn surface
comparisons.documentedSignatureOrBehavior: For a standard A-Token the admin wallet grants MINTER_ROLE to the chosen minter, and only then may that minter mint. For a Wrapped A-Token, MINTER_ROLE is granted to the access_core contract, which locks the origin token and mints 1:1. LIMITS: BURN authority is never documented for a standard A-Token. The documentation states what MINTER_ROLE permits for minting only.
comparisons.observedSignatureOrBehavior: MINTER_ROLE() present, hasRole(bytes32,address) answers, mint selector present, burn selector present
comparisons.impactOnMordant: CleanverseCvaAdapter assumes the issued invoice A-Token exposes the same MINTER_ROLE-gated mint/burn surface proven here for the deployed aUSDC.
comparisons.smallestSponsorQuestion: On a standard A-Token created by /atoken/launch, does MINTER_ROLE authorize both mint(address,uint256) and burn(address,uint256) as it does on aUSDC?

comparisons.documentedSignatureOrBehavior: The platform uses the token's rule together with the holder's A-Pass attributes (tier, subTier, group, subGroup and country tags) to determine whether a wallet may receive or transfer that A-Token. min_tier admits a user whose tier is strictly greater than the configured value. LIMITS: No Solidity policy interface is published. `canTransfer(address,address,address,uint256)` appears nowhere in the documentation; Mordant's ICleanversePolicy is inferred from deployed bytecode, not from a documented ABI.
comparisons.observedSignatureOrBehavior: the probed tuples were rejected with ComplianceFailed(address) [0x8a4e1859], which is consistent with a compliance rule that is not satisfied by those participants
comparisons.impactOnMordant: CleanverseAPassVerifier treats a rejecting policy as a refusal, so for these exact participants every aUSDC settlement path in Mordant (activation proceeds, bond claims, cash redemption) fails closed with SettlementNotReady. conclusions.statement: The canonical Cleanverse Monad testnet contracts exist and answer their documented-by-configuration read surfaces at the pinned block.
conclusions.basis: eth_getCode and eth_call against the A-Pass, aUSDC, AccessCore and factory addresses at one pinned block.

conclusions.statement: No backend/factory selector skew was observable at block 48667706: the Monad A-Token factory implementation exposes both launch selectors.
conclusions.basis: EIP-1967 implementation slot read, followed by a dispatch-table selector scan of the implementation bytecode. A selector scan proves presence in the dispatch table. It does not show that a /atoken/launch application succeeds, which stays NOT PROVEN — WRITE ACTION REQUIRED.

conclusions.statement: BLOCKED — COMPLIANT APASS PROFILE NOT IDENTIFIED: the probed tuples were rejected with ComplianceFailed, which is consistent with a compliance rule that is not satisfied by those participants. Mordant settlement prechecks fail closed for them.
conclusions.basis: eth_call against policy().canTransfer(aUSDC, from, to, 1) for three tuples, including two addresses whose isValidAPass is true; each was rejected with ComplianceFailed(address) [0x8a4e1859]. Bounded to those tuples: it does not establish which attribute is unsatisfied, that the policy rejects every participant, that the policy is faulty, or that holding a valid A-Pass suffices.

conclusions.statement: The Cleanverse CVA/aUSDC rail is not live for Mordant.
conclusions.basis: No A-Pass was issued, no A-Token was launched, no role was granted and no transaction was broadcast. Those are write actions and are out of scope here.

conclusions.statement: Every claim that depends on the protected Cleanverse documentation is unproven in this run.
conclusions.basis: No documentation session access code was available, so the access-gated pages could not be read. Repository notes were not substituted for them.
